rules.statement: Authenticate NuGet package publishing through nuget.org trusted publishing: exchange the job's OIDC token with `NuGet/login` for a short-lived key, and never use a long-lived NuGet API key stored as a secret.
rules.why: A trusted-publishing key only lasts for the job and is scoped to that workflow and environment. A long-lived key in a secret is not.
rules.check: Look for `dotnet nuget push` with `--api-key ${{ secrets.* }}`, or any NuGet API key secret, in a workflow. Flag a publish step that does not get its key from `NuGet/login`.

rules.statement: Split package publishing into a build job with read-only permissions, which builds, tests, packs and uploads the packages, and a separate publish job in a protected environment whose only write permission is `id-token: write`.
rules.why: Write-scoped credentials must stay out of the job that runs third-party build and test code.
rules.check: Look for a publish workflow where one job both builds or tests and pushes. Also flag a build job with write permissions, a publish job with permissions beyond `id-token: write`, or a publish job with no protected `environment:`.

rules.statement: Trigger package publishing only deliberately, from a version tag or a manual `workflow_dispatch` on `main`, never on every push or merge to `main`, and publish a tag only when the tagged commit is already on `main` or a release line.
rules.why: nuget.org versions are permanent, and a version per merge buries the ones a deployment needs. A tag on an unreviewed commit must publish nothing.
rules.check: Look for a publishing workflow triggered by `push` to branches or by `pull_request`. Also flag a tag-triggered publish that never checks the tagged commit is reachable from a protected branch.

rules.statement: Before pushing, make the publish workflow check that all packed packages share one version, that a tag-triggered run's tag names exactly that version, and that a prerelease workflow refuses a release (non-prerelease) version.
rules.why: The family versions packages in lockstep, and the version that ships must be the one the tag names.
rules.check: Look for a publish workflow that pushes packages without checking that the package versions match each other and match the tag. Also flag a prerelease workflow that would push a stable version.

rules.statement: Make the publish job fail when every package of the version is already on nuget.org. Push with `--skip-duplicate` so a rerun completes a partial publish, and push each package's `.snupkg` symbols too.
rules.why: A run on an unchanged version must fail rather than report success for nothing, and a run that failed part way must be able to finish when run again.
rules.check: Look for `dotnet nuget push` without `--skip-duplicate`, and for no check that fails when every package of the version is already published. Also flag `.snupkg` files that are not pushed.
